summary: Increased bleeding risk due to combined anticoagulant/antiplatelet effect.
Risk of serotonin syndrome; combination should be avoided.
Grapefruit inhibits CYP3A4, raising statin levels and myopathy risk.
Additive vasodilation can cause severe, potentially fatal hypotension.
Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4, sharply raising simvastatin levels and rhabdomyolysis risk.
Combined serotonergic and MAO-inhibiting effects can precipitate serotonin syndrome.
Concurrent use raises serum potassium, increasing the risk of dangerous hyperkalemia.
Fluconazole inhibits warfarin metabolism, elevating INR and bleeding risk.
Amiodarone raises digoxin concentrations, increasing the risk of digoxin toxicity.
Thiazide-induced sodium loss reduces lithium clearance, risking lithium toxicity.
Combined AV-nodal suppression can cause bradycardia, heart block, and hypotension.
Ciprofloxacin inhibits theophylline metabolism, raising levels and seizure risk.
Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase, raising azathioprine toxicity and myelosuppression risk.
Metronidazole blocks acetaldehyde metabolism, causing a disulfiram-like reaction.
Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing activation of clopidogrel and its antiplatelet effect.
Rifampin induces hepatic enzymes, lowering hormone levels and contraceptive efficacy.
Calcium chelates doxycycline in the gut, reducing antibiotic absorption and efficacy.
Iron binds levothyroxine in the gut, reducing thyroid hormone absorption.
